title: Scale Intent Contracts and Metric Multiplexor for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Design and implement a contract-based autoscaling layer (Scale Intent Contract) plus a Metric Multiplexor that maps customer intent to a weighted set of target metrics. Goal: provide predictable throughput guarantees for Dedicated fleets while keeping safety limits and cost controls pluggable.
background_and_motivation: We currently have several autoscaler flavors (throughput-target, latency-proportional, headroom crediting) scattered across controllers. Operators and customers need a unified, declarative way to express scaling intent (e.g., 'sustain 1,500 reqs/s at p95 <= 250ms') that the platform can compile into executable policies while preserving safety fences. A Metric Multiplexor allows the control plane to evaluate multiple signals (throughput, p95, queue depth, GPU utilization) concurrently and combine them deterministically.
design_decisions: 1) Intent contract: introduce a lightweight JSON contract schema (see contract example below) that specifies desired SLA, enforcement mode (strict | advisory), and allowable cost envelope. 2) Metric Multiplexor: allow weighting of metrics and selectable combiner (max | weighted_avg | percentile_aggregation). 3) Safety limits: global rate-of-change (ramp), per-tenant surge_budget, and min_reserve fraction on dedicated pools. 4) Algorithms: start with PID-based per-metric controllers + multiplexor output -> slope-limited capacity adjustments; roadmap includes model-predictive controller (MPC) for bursty workloads. 5) Backwards compatibility: default behavior maps existing throughput policies to equivalent intent contracts to avoid customer config churn.
scaling_algorithm_notes: - Multiplexor computes a composite target score using configured weights. - Per-metric PID controllers compute suggested capacity delta. - Composite controller then applies slope-limiting and surge budget checks. - If mode == 'strict' and composite target cannot meet SLA within safety limits, trigger graceful degradation path (fallback_model or rate_limiter) and generate an incident event.
safety_and_failsafe_strategy: - Ramp limits: never increase capacity faster than ramp_rate_pct_per_min unless explicit emergency override. - Surge budget: short-term spike allowance; consumes budget which refills at configured rate. - Min reserve: keep X% of capacity offline for tenant isolation and cold start headroom. - Circuit breaker: if GPU_util > 95% and p95 rising, pause scale-out and escalate to Ops with suggested rollback plan.
observability_and_alerting: Metrics: composite_target_score, per_metric_suggestions, applied_capacity, ramp_consumed_pct, surge_budget_remaining. Dashboards: dedicated/fleet/<fleet-id>/intents, alerts for SLA_violation_predicted, ramp_exhausted, surge_budget_depleted. Link: https://dashboards.internal.redwood.ai/dedicated/intents (internal)
testing_and_validation: - Unit tests for contract parsing and multiplexor math. - Integration test harness simulating Poisson and bursty traffic traces (replay from customer traces). - Canary rollout: 10% of new Dedicated fleets, compare p95 and cost delta vs baseline for 48h. - Benchmarks: target <5% overhead in decision latency; end-to-end reaction time measured (signal->action) under 200ms in staging.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement contract schema + dry-run multiplexor (no active scaling) in staging. Phase 2: implement slope-limited enactment and safety checks; roll out to canary fleets. Phase 3: enable strict mode for opt-in customers; collect telemetry. Phase 4: default behavior migration and deprecation of legacy policies. Rollout docs: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DDED/Scale+Intent+Contracts
open_risks_and_mitigation: Risk: misweighted metrics can oscillate scaling decisions -> Mitigate with conservative default weights, warm-up period, and stabilization window. Risk: cost explosion from poorly set cost caps -> enforce hard deny when cost_cap exceeded. Risk: inter-tenant noisy neighbors -> enforce per-tenant min_reserve and fair-share arbiter.
